idiom_name: class SessionFwd(gate: SessionGate) : Session by gate
implementation_notes: The by-clause generates the forwarder with zero boilerplate: implementing an interface by delegation makes the compiler emit every member as a forward to the stored delegate. The gate is that delegate - it holds the target and the flag, and checks before forwarding - so the check and the forward happen inside one call and no flag read crosses a boundary. Do not try to put the check in overrides on the delegating class: overridden members are used for outside calls, but the delegate's own implementations never see those overrides, so mediation written that way has holes.
pitfalls: Members you override on the delegating class do not affect the delegate's internal self-calls, so a revocation check placed only in overrides is bypassed by the delegate's own member-to-member calls.

Every member of the interface that the gate does not implement itself is forwarded straight to the target by the compiler-generated bridge, so the gate must implement the whole interface or those members stay unrevokable.

The delegate expression is evaluated once and stored, so a wrapper built around a target cannot have its target swapped later; a revocable grant that must be re-pointed needs a gate with a mutable target field.

variants.name: JDK dynamic proxy over InvocationHandler
variants.implementation_notes: On the JVM the delegation can be replaced by reflection: java.lang.reflect.Proxy gives one check point for the whole interface, with a @Volatile flag consulted in the handler before method.invoke(target, args). This variant is unavailable on Kotlin/Native and Kotlin/JS, where the by-clause or a hand-written class is the only route, and it inherits the JDK's behaviour of routing equals, hashCode and toString through the same handler.
pitfalls: Kotlin default methods and extension members are not dispatched like interface methods by the JDK proxy, so parts of a Kotlin interface can behave differently through the proxy than through the by-clause.
The handler must unwrap InvocationTargetException (or the caller sees reflection's wrapper instead of the domain exception); the Kotlin lambda above rethrows whatever reflection throws.
